title: Console: one-click rollback flow for Optimize config versions
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
## Context
We’re adding config version history + rollback for Optimize configuration changes. This ticket covers the **Console UX** for executing a rollback safely and quickly under on-call pressure, with clear blast radius, progress/status, and a post-rollback validation checklist.

This is the on-call path for reversing a known-bad config change (batching/caching/quantization/routing knobs) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private scopes.

## Goals
- Rollback can be executed by authorized operators in < 2 minutes from the Console, with clear confirmation copy.
- Operator clearly understands **what will change** (target version) and **where it will apply** (blast radius / scope).
- Rollback progress is visible and debuggable (correlation IDs, per-target status, deep links to audit events).
- Provide a consistent checklist to validate recovery (dashboards, key metrics, and common pitfalls).

## Non-goals
- Automated rollback without human confirmation.
- Partial rollback of individual fields (whole-config rollback only; exceptions documented elsewhere).

## UX Requirements
### Entry points
1) Version History page (ENG-4825): "Rollback" button on a prior known-good version.
2) Current/active config details view: "Rollback" → opens version picker modal.

### Confirmation modal (hard requirement)
Show the following *before* starting rollback:
- **Target version**: Version ID, created time, author, reason/ticket link (if present).
- **Current version** (the version being replaced).
- **Blast radius** (computed from scope):
  - Customer / tenant
  - Deployment mode: Hosted | Dedicated | Private
  - Environment (prod/staging) where applicable
  - Region(s)
  - Cluster(s) (if the scope is cluster-specific)
  - Route(s) + model(s)
- **Expected behavior + warnings** (static copy + dynamic callouts):
  - “Rollback re-applies the full configuration for the selected version.”
  - “Rollback may invalidate caches and trigger warmup; watch p95 latency and error rate during propagation.”
  - If multiple regions/clusters: “Propagation is rolling; requests may briefly run mixed versions until completion.”
- **Permission gating**
  - If user lacks `optimize.config.rollback`, hide CTA and show “Request access” link.
- **Justification input**
  - Required for enterprise tenants and prod scopes: free-text “Why are you rolling back?”
  - Optional “Link ticket” field (Linear/Jira URL). If provided, included in rollback request metadata.
- CTA: "Rollback to vX" (destructive).
- Secondary: Cancel.

### Progress / status view (hard requirement)
After confirmation, transition to a dedicated rollback status page/panel with:
- Overall state: Queued → Applying → Propagating → Completed / Failed / Partially completed.
- Time started, elapsed time.
- **Request ID / Correlation ID** (copyable), and link to audit log entry.
- Per-target status table if rollout fanout exists (e.g., region/cluster targets):
  - Target (region/cluster)
  - State
  - Last update time
  - Error message (human readable) + "View details" (includes raw error code)
- Primary actions:
  - If failed: "Retry rollback" (idempotent with new idempotency key)
  - "View runbook" deep link
  - "Open incident" (link to incident template; optional but nice-to-have for Phase 1)

### Post-rollback validation checklist (hard requirement)
When rollback reaches Completed (or Partially completed), show a checklist with:
- Confirm active version shows the rolled-back version everywhere expected (deep link to version history filtered by scope)
- Check dashboards (deep links):
  - Latency (p50/p95) by route/model
  - Error rate (5xx, timeouts)
  - Saturation / GPU utilization (where available)
  - Config-apply health dashboard (ENG-4828)
- Suggested validation window: “Monitor for 10–15 minutes.”
- Common pitfalls callout:
  - Some improvements may lag until cache warmup completes
  - Client-side retries can mask ongoing elevated errors; check server-side counters
- Comms template stub (collapsed): “We rolled back Optimize config to vX due to …; monitoring until …”

## Data / API expectations
- Console uses rollback endpoint (ENG-4823) and job/status endpoints (Console backend endpoints in PR-10502; may be a new /operations route).
- Need a blast radius object from backend OR a deterministic client-side renderer based on scope fields from version metadata.
  - Current plan: backend returns a normalized `scope_summary` string + structured fields; Console renders string + chips.
  - If backend is not ready, we can render from the version’s scope fields returned by list/get.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] From version history, operator can click Rollback on a prior version and see confirmation modal with:
  - [ ] target version + current version
  - [ ] blast radius summary
  - [ ] required justification (prod + enterprise)
  - [ ] permission gating
- [ ] On confirm, rollback request is issued with idempotency key and operator metadata.
- [ ] Status view updates automatically until terminal state (polling acceptable in Phase 1; SSE optional).
- [ ] Status view shows correlation ID and deep link to audit events.
- [ ] Terminal state displays post-rollback checklist with dashboard links.
- [ ] All copy reviewed by PM (Marissa Cole) + SRE (Rafael Mendes) + Design (Kenji Nakamura).
- [ ] Basic accessibility: focus trap in modal, keyboard navigation, and screen-reader labels for status.

## Implementation Notes
- UI should treat rollback as an async operation; never block the UI while waiting for propagation.
- If rollback returns “partial propagation / mixed state”:
  - show “Partially completed” state and list failed targets with recommended actions (retry or escalate).
- Ensure we do not expose sensitive config payloads in the confirmation modal by default; diff/preview lives in compare view (ENG-4825). The rollback confirmation should reference “View diff” link that returns to compare.

## Links
- PRD: Confluence: Safe apply + rollback PRD (Marissa)
- Design notes: Drive: rollback UX wire notes (Kenji)
- Runbook: Confluence: Rollback Optimize config in production (Rafael)
- Related PRs:
  - redwood/pr-10502-console-rollback-flow-and-notifications (in progress)
  - redwood/pr-10488-console-backend-version-history-endpoints

## Open Questions
1) Do we require justification for *all* prod rollbacks or only enterprise tenants? (PM leaning: required for prod scopes regardless of tenant type; confirm with Fiona/McCarthy.)
2) For Dedicated: do we show “blast radius” as cluster+region only, or also include dedicated pool ID? (Need input from SRE.)
3) Can status updates be pushed (websocket/SSE) in Phase 2, or is polling good enough for GA?

## Execution Plan
- Milestone 1: Confirmation modal + API call wiring + basic polling status
- Milestone 2: Blast radius renderer + audit deep link + checklist/dashboard links
- Milestone 3: Failure/partial propagation UX + retry path + a11y pass

## Activity / Updates
- 2025-02-03 (Hannah Rivera): Implemented initial rollback modal (copy stub) + permission gating behind feature flag `optimizeRollbackUI`.
- 2025-02-06 (Kenji Nakamura): Reviewed modal layout; requested blast-radius chips and clearer destructive CTA copy (“Rollback to v12”).
- 2025-02-10 (Rafael Mendes): Requested status page include correlation ID and direct link to runbook section “Verify recovery” + dashboard links for p95 and 5xx.
- 2025-02-12 (Chloe Martin): Backend can return operation status via `/v1/optimize/config/operations/{id}`; polling cadence recommended 2s→5s backoff.
- 2025-02-17 (Allison Grant): Ensure audit deep link uses canonical event id, not request id; request id should remain copyable for incident channels.

## Comments
- Dylan Brooks (2025-02-05): Please keep the on-call path “one screen deep”: after confirmation, always land on the status view with a stable URL so it can be pasted into Slack/incident threads.
- Marissa Cole (2025-02-11): Justification should be required for prod rollbacks; ticket link optional but highly encouraged. Copy should say “This action reverts to a prior known-good config version.”
- Fiona McCarthy (2025-02-13): Justification + ticket link should be captured into audit metadata; do not log raw config payloads in audit events.
- Kenji Nakamura (2025-02-18): Add a compact “Blast radius: {customer} · {mode} · {regions} · {routes/models}” single-line summary for fast scanning; chips below for details.
